scoring_justification: The paper reports qualitative trends (LO-phonon peak ordering, X7 negligible, hot-phonon effect on X6 decay) without a single numeric metric. Recomputing from raw artifacts would require a full EMC simulation (hours of compute) in the verifier sandbox, which is infeasible. Structural checks on the output CSVs are appropriate and faithful to the paper's claims.

output_contract.notes: Structural audit checks ordering of peak q-vectors (q_Γ < q_L < q_X7 < q_X6), minimal X7 contribution, and slower X6 decay with hot phonons. Exact numerical values are not required.

hidden_assets.source_provenance: Paper equations (2)-(3), Fig.5 description, and the statement about X7 contribution being negligible; hot-phonon effect slowing X6 decay from paper discussion.
hidden_assets.generation_method: Extracted the qualitative claims (peak q ordering, X7 weakest, hot phonons cause slower X6 decay) directly from the paper's text and figures. No fabricated numbers.
hidden_assets.why_not_fabricated: These conditions reproduce the paper's own reported physical behavior; failing them means the reproduction did not capture the key results.

steps.description: Check that X6 valley population decays more slowly when hot_phonons=true than when false.
Verify peak q ordering (q_Gamma < q_L < q_X7 < q_X6) and X7 contribution is smallest.
Verify that distributions broaden and overlap more compared to 2ps: peak q range shrinks and peak-to-valley ratio decreases.
